APPROVED RP-04 subprocess policy: trusted same-capability children inherit the ambient environment for compatibility. Rebar never mutates global os.environ to install adapter secrets; Rebar-materialized static credentials are overlaid only onto the owning child; unrelated sibling children remove only exact secret variable names declared by other Rebar adapters; unknown ambient variables and native Git/SSH/AWS credential-process/proxy/CA chains remain intact. Deployment step/container/service scoping is the primary security boundary. This protects against accidental propagation of Rebar-known credentials; it is not a process sandbox. Strict/hermetic mode is outside initial scope.

APPROVED RP-04 scope decision: no automatic local Python keyring adapter and no built-in cloud-secret retrieval in the initial implementation. Local use continues through provider-native helpers or environment injection. A later optional adapter requires concrete demand and a separate evidence-backed design decision.

The research artifact was reconciled to remove stale strict-allowlist and arbitrary constructed-client language. Later verification must cover ambient/unknown-variable inheritance, owning-child overlay, exact sibling removal, no global-environment mutation, and canary non-leakage. Gitleaks scanned .joe-janitor with --no-git --redact after the update and found no leaks. No RP-04 design choices remain pending inside the researched scope; the research-summary confirmation gate remains before ADR drafting.
